cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: The A button swings the sword.

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle costs 60 rupees in the documents: it can be bought for 60 Rupees through a door one screen west of the Fairy Fountain route in the 1st Quest, and a shop in the 2nd Quest also sells it for 60 rupees.

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need five Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items document and the Hyrule 3 cave description. One Quest 1 overworld walkthrough says six Heart Containers are needed for the same sword.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level 3 of the first quest, you can find the Raft, which is located down the stairwell past the Compass room. The Level 3 objectives also include obtaining a Heart Container and the third Triforce piece.

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4 and is four times as powerful as the wooden sword, making it the most powerful sword in the game.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: According to the Raft item entry, Link can cross lakes and oceans using the Raft, but it can only be used at a Dock, and neither of the 'double docks' triggers raft use.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. Fairies refill your hearts: a fairy drop fills 3 of Link's hearts, and in the fairy ponds a fairy fills all your heart meters.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: The Money Making Game is a gambling option in the game. You can find its cave by bombing the cliff wall just left of center in Hyrule 2 section A-5, or by walking into the tree in Hyrule 1 section D-2, or bombing along the middle of the north wall in Hyrule 6 section C-5.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: In Section 2 of the overworld (Hyrule 2, 2nd Quest), D-4 is a shop where you can buy Arrows for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" when you start the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents describe the name as "Zelda"; they do not explicitly say whether the all-caps form "ZELDA" triggers the same cheat.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle can be bought for 60 Rupees in a shop reached from the Fairy Fountain: walk three screens south then two screens west, use a bomb to find 30 Rupees, then return to the Fountain and go south two and east four screens to find another 30 Rupees, then go one screen west and enter the door. It throws a flame that can light dark dungeon rooms, burn bushes in the overworld, and damage enemies, but can only be used once per screen.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
cases.answer: The boss of Level 1 in the first quest is Aquamentus. You must strike his head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between the energy orbs he emits from his horn. Only the Magical Shield absorbs those orbs, and firing sword beams can hit any part of his body.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The dragon boss Aquamentus has 6 HP and shoots fireballs that split in three directions, which can only be blocked by the Magical Shield. It is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows, and can also be killed by two Bombs.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: Each Gleeok head must be stabbed until it flies freely around the room, and the free head is still a threat that cannot be defeated. You must destroy every attached head to beat Gleeok; the two-headed boss in Quest 1 Dungeon 4, the four-headed boss in Quest 1 Dungeon 8, and the four-headed boss in Quest 2 Dungeon 7 all follow this strategy, and defeating it earns a Heart Container.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. Press the B button to use your selected subweapon, such as the Magical Wand, which fires magical blasts.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword, which is the attack. The B button is used for subweapons, not for attacking with the sword.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. Press the B button to use your equipped subweapon.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map, change subweapon, and see inventory. Press Start again to return from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes, bombs can blast holes in weak walls. The item description says the bomb can be used to kill enemies or blast holes in weak walls. Walkthroughs also instruct bombing walls to reveal hidden passages.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Press the B button to use your subweapon. Only one item can be assigned to B at a time, and you change that assignment on the sub-screen, which you open with Start. Select the subweapon you want in the sub-screen's blue box.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. You can also press the B button to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: Fairy heals 3 hearts, and in fairy ponds it fills all hearts. A Water of Life completely refills your life bar, and a medicine woman in Hyrule 7 sells Red Potions and Water of Life.

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: Several money sources are documented: the Money Making Game is in a cave reached by bombing the rock face immediately left of the start screen (zelda1:cheats:004). In the 2nd Quest, you can play it by walking inside the tree at Hyrule 1 D-2 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003), or find it by bombing the north wall of Hyrule 6 C-5 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-6:003). Hyrule 1 B-4 (1st Quest) and B-3 (2nd Quest) also have caves giving 30 Rupees, and Hyrule 8 B-2 leads to 10 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003, zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:002).

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: The most powerful sword in the game is the Magic Sword, which deals 4 damage and is four times as powerful as the Wooden Sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: One cheat says that when you enter the first dungeon, immediately leave and come back, and the locked door will open. Each key opens one door, and Link can carry up to nine keys until he obtains the magic key.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: Bomb every wall that does not contain a door, since passageways leading further into the dungeon are typically found that way. Also, unmarked rooms or the "eyes" on the dungeon map can hold passages to explore.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon; Link must attack each head, and when a head takes enough damage it detaches and flies around the room. The flying heads cannot be hurt, so dodge their projectiles and focus on the heads still attached to the body. Keep stabbing the attached heads until every one is disconnected.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: In Quest 1 overworld, fight and defeat the Moblins in the nearby area until they drop Bombs that you can collect. Quest 2 overworld also lists getting Bombs as a step, and the Quest 1 Dungeon 6 resupply notes replacement Bombs from a man found one screen north and two screens east of a Water of Life woman.

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, Dungeon 1, the Bow is found in room O-1, which has Traps in each corner and a stairwell in the center surrounded by blocks. Push the left-most block aside to enter the stairwell, where you'll find the Bow. You'll need to purchase Arrows to use it, unless you already bought them before finding the Bow.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: To save your game, choose "SAVE" on the Game Over screen using Select and then press Start; this stores your accomplishments until you next play. Alternatively, you can press Up (D-pad) and A simultaneously on the second controller from the sub-screen menu to quickly access the Save Screen.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: You can get a Heart Container, which permanently adds an extra heart to Link's life meter. In Quest 1, one is found by burning a fifth tree from the right on a screen on the Lake Hylia coast, and another by bombing a huge rock at the foot of the eastern mountains. In Quest 2, you can push a tombstone in the Graveyard to get a Heart Container. Fairies also restore hearts, filling 3 hearts or all hearts in fairy ponds.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes. A Magical Shield is sold in shops, which reflects more attacks than the starting Small Shield. In Quest 1, a shop reached by burning a tree after the Fairy Fountain sells one for 90 Rupees. In the 2nd Quest overworld, shops also sell it for 90, 130, or 160 Rupees depending on location.

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: Dark rooms can be lit with candles: the Blue Candle lights them but can only be used once per screen, while the Red Candle has the same effect with no per-screen limit. The Dungeon 4 walkthrough also suggests using the Blue Candle to light the dark rooms.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air. Jump height is fixed, so tapping or holding A gives the same height.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points to throw.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump toward and cling to a wall, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back toward it. Done correctly, you rise and cling to the wall higher than where you started, and repeating it can take you to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead, who attacks as soon as you enter the hall. Bomberhead's spinning weapon has better reach than Barbarian's, so you cannot duck below it.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The boss of Stage 3-3 (Act III) is Basaquer, who leaps back and forth across the room and shoots trios of darts.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
cases.answer: The Fire Wheel surrounds Ryu with a circle of fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts him, and it disappears after five seconds of use. It requires no spirit points to use, but it replaces any secondary weapon you currently hold.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press B to attack by swinging your sword, and you can attack low by squatting when you attack. Hold Up on the D-pad while pressing B to use your secondary weapon, which needs enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: The documents do not explicitly describe a 'ninpo' item. The closest related facts are that Spirit Points tiles (blue give 5, red give 10) are needed to use secondary weapons, and tiles can be collected in the stages, such as the red Spirit Points tile in Stage 2-1 and the one from the first insect in Stage 2-2.

cases.question: how do i heal?
cases.answer: The documents mention health-restoring potions that you can collect in the stages: in Stage 4-2, a lamp on the left holds a potion that restores some lost health, and in Stage 3-1, the item over a small dock segment is a health-restoring potion. Stage 2-2 has an insect item holding a health restoring potion, and Stage 5-2 has a candle above the first potion that contains a health restoring potion.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: Losing to any of the final bosses sends you back to 6-1, regardless of how many lives you have left. Defeated bosses stay dead, so you won't have to face them again once you return to this stage.
